test_suite.feature: Customer Account Creation — Customer Detail page in Insert/Account-Creation mode (Scan And Shop / "Customer & Order Analysis" module, M1.3, user story US-CI-06)
test_suite.summary: This specification covers manual test cases for the Customer Account Creation form, derived strictly from two BRD sources: Scan_And_Shop_BRD_Overview (M1.3, US-CI-06; resolution R5) and the Customer Detail sub-page document (§1.0 Trigger/Precondition, §1.1 Endpoint, §1.2 Page Properties, §2 Controls, §3.1 Data Source, §5.1 Save Customer Details event with 8 validations + 8 actions). Behaviour under test is limited to what is explicitly documented: mandatory First/Last name, mandatory and format-checked Email, brand-scoped Email uniqueness, minimum-10-digit Home and Mobile phone rules, phone and country-code normalisation on Save, default Gender = Male, default Country = United States of America, and the post-Save context stamping (BrandID, CustomerBrand link, event copy, UserParam.CurrentCustomerID). A critical conflict is recorded and treated per the BRD: the Feature Under Test supplied for this task includes a Terms & Conditions acceptance gate that enables the Save button, but BOTH BRD sources explicitly DE-SCOPE Terms acceptance under R5 (Overview R5 and Resolution Log; Customer Detail §1, §2, §5.1 validation #40, §5.1 action #40, §5.2, CC-3). No Terms-gated Save behaviour is authored as expected behaviour; R5 removal is verified by regression-style absence checks (TC-033, TC-034) and the conflict is raised under requirement_gaps. Techniques applied: Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis, Decision Table Testing, State Transition Testing, Use Case Testing, Checklist-based Testing (for the UI check), and Error Guessing. Prioritisation is risk-based (High/Medium/Low); customer creation and email integrity are the highest-risk areas of this CRM entry flow.
test_suite.coverage: Functional requirements identified: 18 (FR-01 open form in Insert mode with brand context — §1.0/§1.1/§1.2, US-CI-03; FR-02 capture Contact Information fields — §2; FR-03 capture Address Information fields — §2; FR-04 First Name required — §5.1 #50; FR-05 Last Name required — §5.1 #60; FR-06 Email required/not null — §5.1 #30; FR-07 Email format valid — §5.1 #70; FR-08 Email unique within brand — §5.1 #80, §3.1; FR-09 Home Phone minimum 10 digits — §5.1 #10; FR-10 Mobile/Cell Phone minimum 10 digits — §5.1 #20; FR-11 default Gender = Male — §2; FR-12 default Country = United States of America — §2; FR-13 phone number normalisation on Save — §5.1 actions #10/#20, §3.1 FormattedCellPhone; FR-14 country-code normalisation on Save — §5.1 action #30; FR-15 Save commit chain: stamp BrandID, create CustomerBrand link, copy event, set CurrentCustomerID — §5.1 actions #5/#8/#50/#60, §1.0 postcondition; FR-16 Save action creates the customer — §2 Action, US-CI-06; FR-17 continue flow with the new customer set as current into the scan/shop workspace — §1.0 postcondition, US-CI-05; FR-18 Terms acceptance de-scoped: no Terms UI and Save not Terms-gated — Overview R5, §2, §5.1 #40). Total test cases generated: 41 (TC-001..TC-041). Coverage by requirement: FR-01 → TC-036, TC-029; FR-02 → TC-001, TC-007, TC-035; FR-03 → TC-007, TC-035; FR-04 → TC-002, TC-018; FR-05 → TC-003, TC-018; FR-06 → TC-004, TC-029; FR-07 → TC-005, TC-006, TC-019, TC-037; FR-08 → TC-020, TC-025, TC-026, TC-038; FR-09 → TC-011, TC-012, TC-013, TC-021, TC-039; FR-10 → TC-014, TC-015, TC-016, TC-039; FR-11 → TC-009, TC-022, TC-024; FR-12 → TC-010, TC-023, TC-024; FR-13 → TC-007, TC-027, TC-039; FR-14 → TC-010, TC-028; FR-15 → TC-030; FR-16 → TC-001, TC-017, TC-040; FR-17 → TC-031, TC-032; FR-18 → TC-033, TC-034. Coverage by test design technique: Equivalence Partitioning = 19 (TC-001..TC-010, TC-022, TC-023, TC-024, TC-025, TC-026, TC-027, TC-028, TC-033, TC-034); Boundary Value Analysis = 6 (TC-011..TC-016); Decision Table Testing = 5 (TC-017..TC-021); State Transition Testing = 2 (TC-029, TC-030); Use Case Testing = 3 (TC-031, TC-032, TC-036); Checklist-based Testing = 1 (TC-035); Error Guessing = 5 (TC-037..TC-041). Non-functional areas (Security/authorization, Performance, Accessibility, Compatibility, Reliability) are not documented in the BRD and are reported under requirement_gaps rather than tested.

requirement_gaps.gap: CRITICAL CONFLICT. The Feature Under Test states "Users must accept the Terms before the Save button becomes enabled" and describes an embedded Store Terms section and Privacy Policy link. Both BRD sources DE-SCOPE this under R5 (Overview R5 and Resolution Log; Customer Detail §1, §2, §5.1 validation #40 removed, §5.1 action #40 removed, §5.2, CC-3). The two inputs contradict each other; the authoritative source must be confirmed before any Terms-gated Save behaviour can be specified.

Save button enable/disable behaviour is undocumented in scope. The BRD models Save as validate-on-click (§5.1: 8 validations then commit); it defines no dynamic enabling/disabling of the Save control. The "Save becomes enabled" behaviour cannot be verified against the BRD.

It is not stated whether the minimum-10-digit rules (§5.1 #10 Home, #20 Cell) fire only when a value is entered. Both phone fields are optional (§2), implying conditional application, but this is not explicit.

No maximum length or upper boundary is documented for phone numbers; only "10 Digits Min" is stated. The normalisation expression (§3.1 FormattedCellPhone) formats only the first 10 digits, leaving 11+ digit handling undefined.
Exact user-facing validation/error message text is not specified. §5.1 lists rule names only (e.g., "First Name Missing", "Duplicate Brand Email Address"), not displayed messages.
No success confirmation behaviour is documented (no success message, redirect target, or confirmation UI). The §1.0 postcondition describes context stamping and flow continuation only.

Gender and Country are marked required (*) in §2, but there is NO Save validation for either among the 8 validations in §5.1. It is unclear whether "required" is enforced solely by the pre-filled defaults or whether clearing them (if possible) is blocked at Save.
The enumerated valid Gender values (beyond default Male) and the full Country list are sourced externally (Global Configuration / Rest Countries) and are not listed in these documents.
The definition of a "valid" email format (§5.1 #70) is unspecified (RFC compliance, permitted TLDs, case-sensitivity, whitespace handling).
No field-length limits, character-set restrictions, or format rules are documented for First Name, Last Name, Title, Address, City, State, or Postal Code.
Duplicate-email matching semantics are not specified: whether the §5.1 #80 check is case-insensitive and/or trims whitespace before comparison.
A 'Close' literal exists in the data source (§3.1 'Close' AS CloseText), but §2.B states the only action control is Save. The existence/behaviour of a Close/Cancel control on the form is ambiguous.

Behaviour on server failure, partial save, duplicate double-submit, or concurrency (two associates creating the same brand email simultaneously) is not documented; §5.1 #80 is a check-then-insert with no stated race protection.

No audit requirement is documented for account creation on this page beyond generic AddedBy/AddedOn/ChangedBy/ChangedOn columns in §3.1; no explicit audit/event-history acceptance criteria are stated.

Non-functional requirements are absent: Security/authorization (which roles may create customers; unauthenticated/missing brand-context access), Performance, Accessibility (keyboard, focus order, labels/ARIA, contrast), Compatibility (browsers/devices), and Reliability are not specified anywhere in the BRD.
Sub-account handling is ambiguous: §3.1 inherits a parent email via LEFT JOIN (isnull(C2.Email, C.Email)); interaction between ParentCustomerID and the brand duplicate-email check is undocumented.

assumptions.assumption: The BRD is authoritative over the Feature Under Test wherever they conflict (per the task constraint to use only documented information). Accordingly, Terms & Conditions acceptance is OUT OF SCOPE (R5) and Save is NOT gated by Terms.
The minimum-10-digit phone rules are assumed to apply only when a phone value is entered, because Home Phone and Mobile Phone are optional (§2). TC-008, TC-012, and TC-015 rely on this.

Preconditions common to all cases: the user is authenticated as a store associate / back-office user, a brand context is set (UserParam.CurrentOrderBrandID), and the Customer Detail page is opened in Insert (Account Creation) mode via Create Account at ?$mode=Insert&BrandID={CurrentOrderBrandID} (§1.0, §1.1, §1.2).
"Valid email format" is assumed to mean a conventional local-part@domain.tld structure for designing positive/negative format cases, pending RG-09.

Email uniqueness is enforced per brand only (§5.1 #80 combined with the brand-scoped WHERE clause in §3.1), so the same email may exist under a different brand. TC-026 relies on this and must be re-baselined if RG-13 clarification differs.
Phone display normalisation to the US pattern "(xxx) xxx-xxxx" (§3.1 FormattedCellPhone; §5.1 actions #10/#20) is assumed to be the expected stored/displayed format.

As no distinct success UI is documented (RG-06), successful creation is verified via documented postconditions: the new Customer is stamped to the brand, a CustomerBrand link is created, and UserParam.CurrentCustomerID is set to the new customer (§1.0, §5.1 actions).

Error Guessing cases target the robustness of documented validations (§5.1 #10/#20/#70/#80) using inputs likely to expose defects; where the precise handling is unspecified, the expected result is expressed against the documented rule and cross-referenced to the relevant gap.

risks.risk: Brand-scoped email uniqueness (§5.1 #80). Failure allows duplicate customer records within a brand, corrupting the CRM source of truth and downstream order/scan association. Case-insensitivity and concurrency are unspecified, widening the failure surface.
Mandatory field enforcement and customer commit (§5.1 #30/#50/#60; actions). Failure creates incomplete or uncontactable customer records that block or misroute the assisted scan/shop flow.

Terms de-scope (R5) vs the supplied feature spec. If the removed Terms gate (validation #40/action #40) is not fully removed, Save may be blocked or perform obsolete initialisation, breaking creation for all users.

Post-Save context stamping (§5.1 actions #5/#8/#50/#60). If BrandID, the CustomerBrand link, or CurrentCustomerID is not set correctly, the new customer is not brand-scoped or the flow does not continue with them selected.
Undocumented authorization. Without a defined access model, unauthorized roles or unauthenticated/missing-brand access could create or tamper with customer records.
Phone validation and normalisation (§5.1 #10/#20, actions #10/#20). Incorrect digit-count handling or truncation of 11+ digit input yields malformed phone data used later for contact.
Email format validation (§5.1 #70). An unclear format definition risks both false rejects (valid emails blocked) and false accepts (malformed emails stored).
Defaults vs required enforcement for Gender/Country. With no Save validation, clearing a default (if possible) could persist an empty "required" field.
Absent error and success messaging. Users may not understand why Save failed or whether creation succeeded, causing rework or duplicate attempts.
UI layout/labels/grouping (§2). Cosmetic or labelling defects have low functional impact but affect usability.
Country-code normalisation for non-default countries (§5.1 action #30) with an unlisted country set; low frequency in the primary US-default flow.

recommendations.recommendation: Resolve the Terms conflict authoritatively: confirm R5 in the Feature Under Test, remove the Terms/Save-enablement wording, and explicitly state that Save is validate-on-click and always enabled (or define exact enable/disable rules if a gate is reinstated).

Specify phone rules precisely: whether the 10-digit minimum applies only when a value is entered, the permitted character set, the maximum length, and the handling of input beyond 10 digits (reject vs truncate vs store).
Document exact validation/error message text for each rule (§5.1 #10/#20/#30/#50/#60/#70/#80) and define the success confirmation behaviour (message and/or navigation target).
Clarify enforcement of required Gender and Country: either add explicit Save validations or state that required-ness is guaranteed by non-clearable defaults.
Define the email format acceptance criteria and the duplicate-match semantics (case-insensitivity, whitespace trimming) so uniqueness and format checks are unambiguous and testable.
Add field constraints (max length, allowed characters) for all free-text fields to enable boundary and robustness testing.
Specify duplicate-submit and concurrency handling for the check-then-insert email uniqueness path (e.g., unique constraint, idempotent Save, disable-on-submit).

Add non-functional requirements: an authorization model (roles permitted to create customers; unauthenticated/missing brand-context behaviour), plus accessibility, performance, compatibility, and reliability targets.
Clarify the presence/behaviour of a Close/Cancel control and the sub-account (ParentCustomerID) email-inheritance interaction with the brand duplicate-email rule.
State audit acceptance criteria for account creation (what is recorded, where, and whether it is user-verifiable).

test_case.requirement_reference: US-CI-06; Customer Detail §2 (Controls), §5.1 (Save Customer Details); FR-16, FR-11, FR-12
test_case.title: Create customer with all valid mandatory fields and default Gender/Country
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode with brand context set (AS-03). No existing customer with the test email in the current brand.
test_case.test_data: First Name = "John"; Last Name = "Miller"; Email = "john.miller@example.com"; Gender = Male (default); Country = United States of America (default); optional fields blank.
test_case.steps: Enter First and Last Name. Enter a valid, brand-unique Email. Leave Gender and Country at defaults. Click Save.
test_case.expected_result: All 8 validations pass; the Customer is committed and stamped to the current brand (BrandID = CurrentOrderBrandID); a CustomerBrand link is created; UserParam.CurrentCustomerID is set to the new customer and the flow continues with that customer selected (AS-07).

test_case.preconditions: Email E exists for a customer under Brand A. The current order brand context is Brand B (AS-05). Form open in Insert mode for Brand B.
test_case.test_data: First = "Paul"; Last = "Reed"; Email = E; current brand = Brand B.
test_case.steps: Confirm the current order brand is Brand B (different from where E exists). Enter valid names and email E. Click Save.
test_case.expected_result: Save succeeds; the duplicate-email validation is brand-scoped, so E may exist once per brand. Re-baseline if RG-13 clarification changes uniqueness scope.

test_case.requirement_reference: Customer Detail §5.1 action #20, §3.1 FormattedCellPhone; FR-13
test_case.title: Mobile phone is normalised to the "(xxx) xxx-xxxx" format after Save

test_case.title: Country code is normalised from the brand/country on Save

test_case.requirement_reference: Customer Detail §1.2 (Insert mode), §5.1 validation #30; FR-01, FR-06
test_case.title: State transition — invalid Save keeps the form active, then correction commits
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode (AS-03). States: S1 Empty Insert form → S2 Data Entered → S3 Validation Failed → S4 Committed.
test_case.test_data: Step-1 invalid: First = "Kate"; Last = "Doe"; Email = "" (empty). Step-2 correction: Email = "kate.doe@example.com".
test_case.steps: From S1, enter names but leave Email empty (S2). Click Save — expect transition to S3 (Validation Failed). Enter a valid Email. Click Save again — expect transition to S4 (Committed).
test_case.expected_result: The first Save transitions to Validation Failed (blocked by #30, no commit, form remains editable with data retained); after correction, Save transitions to Committed and the customer is created and set as current. No invalid intermediate state persists a customer.

test_case.requirement_reference: Customer Detail §5.1 actions #5/#8/#10/#20/#30/#50/#60, §1.0 postcondition; FR-15; (action #40 removed — R5)
test_case.title: State transition — successful Save stamps brand context and current customer
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode (AS-03). Transition: Data Entered (valid) → Committed → Current-customer context established.
test_case.test_data: First = "Mark"; Last = "Lane"; Email = "mark.lane@example.com".
test_case.steps: Enter valid mandatory fields. Click Save. Observe the resulting context.
test_case.expected_result: On the transition to Committed, the Save actions execute in order: BrandID stamped to CurrentBrandID (#5), CustomerBrand link inserted (#8), phone/country-code normalised (#10/#20/#30), event copied (#50), and UserParam.CurrentCustomerID set to the new customer (#60). The flow continues with the new customer selected (AS-07). Action #40 (Terms) is de-scoped per R5 and must NOT execute.

test_case.requirement_reference: Overview US-CI-01, US-CI-02, US-CI-03, US-CI-06, US-CI-05; Customer Detail §1.0; FR-17
test_case.title: End-to-end — search with no match, create account, and continue into the scan/shop flow
test_case.preconditions: User authenticated with a brand context set (AS-03). Customer Search panel accessible (US-CI-01).
test_case.test_data: Search: First = "Zoe", Last = "West" (no existing match). Create: First = "Zoe"; Last = "West"; Email = "zoe.west@example.com".
test_case.steps: Open the Customer Search panel (US-CI-01). Search by first + last name returning no match (US-CI-02). Click Create Account to branch to the form (US-CI-03 → US-CI-06). Complete the mandatory fields and click Save. Observe that the new customer becomes the current customer.
test_case.expected_result: The customer is created, stamped to the brand, linked via CustomerBrand, and set as UserParam.CurrentCustomerID; the associate continues with the new customer selected, entering the downstream scan/shop workspace (as with an existing customer via Search Results → Scan, US-CI-05).

test_case.requirement_reference: Overview US-CI-01, US-CI-03; Customer Detail §1.0; FR-01, FR-17
test_case.title: End-to-end — branch directly to Create Account from the search entry (no search run)
test_case.preconditions: User authenticated with brand context set (AS-03). Customer Search panel open; no search executed (US-CI-01 states no search runs automatically on open).
test_case.test_data: First = "Ben"; Last = "Ford"; Email = "ben.ford@example.com".
test_case.steps: Open the Customer Search panel. Without running a search, click Create Account (US-CI-03, no match required). Complete mandatory fields on the form. Click Save.
test_case.expected_result: The Account Creation form opens in Insert mode with the brand context; the customer is created and set as current, confirming Create Account is reachable without first running a search.

test_case.requirement_reference: Overview R5; Customer Detail §2 (Terms row removed), §5.1 validation #40 removed; FR-18; RG-01
test_case.title: R5 verification — the embedded Store Terms section and Privacy Policy link are NOT present

test_case.test_data: None (UI inspection).
test_case.steps: Open the Account Creation form. Inspect for an embedded "{Brand} Store Terms" block, a Privacy Policy link, and any accept-terms control.
test_case.expected_result: No Store Terms block, Privacy Policy link, or acceptance control is present, consistent with R5. If any Terms UI appears, raise a defect/clarification against RG-01 (feature-vs-BRD conflict).

test_case.requirement_reference: Overview R5; Customer Detail §5.1 validation #40 removed; FR-18; RG-01, RG-02
test_case.title: R5 verification — Save is NOT gated by Terms acceptance
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode (AS-03). Addresses RG-01/RG-02 (feature claims Save is Terms-gated; BRD removes the gate).
test_case.test_data: First = "Ada"; Last = "Nash"; Email = "ada.nash@example.com"; no terms interaction available/performed.
test_case.steps: Enter only the mandatory contact fields. Without accepting any Terms (none should exist), click Save.
test_case.expected_result: Save proceeds and creates the customer using only the documented validations (#10, #20, #30, #50, #60, #70, #80); no IsTermsAccepted validation (#40) blocks Save. Any Terms-based blocking indicates the feature-vs-BRD conflict (RG-01).

test_case.title: UI validation — mandatory markers and field grouping match the BRD

test_case.title: Precondition/navigation — form opens in Insert mode with the current brand context

test_case.requirement_reference: Customer Detail §5.1 validations #70, #80; FR-07, FR-08; RG-09, RG-11; AS-08
test_case.title: Error guessing — Email with leading/trailing whitespace
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode (AS-03). Probes robustness of the email format (#70) and duplicate (#80) rules.
test_case.test_data: First = "Sam"; Last = "Doe"; Email = " sam.doe@example.com " (leading and trailing spaces); a customer with "sam.doe@example.com" may or may not already exist in the brand.
test_case.steps: Enter valid names. Enter the Email with surrounding spaces. Click Save. If a trimmed duplicate exists, observe whether it is detected.
test_case.expected_result: Behaviour is per the documented format (#70) and duplicate (#80) rules. Since whitespace/trim handling is unspecified (RG-09/RG-11), record the actual result: ideally the email is trimmed and treated consistently for both format and uniqueness. Any inconsistency (e.g., stored with spaces or bypassing the duplicate check) is a defect/clarification item.

test_case.requirement_reference: Customer Detail §5.1 validation #80; FR-08; RG-11; AS-08
test_case.title: Error guessing — duplicate email differing only by letter case
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode (AS-03). A customer with "john.doe@example.com" already exists in the current brand.
test_case.test_data: First = "John"; Last = "Doe"; Email = "John.Doe@EXAMPLE.com" (same address, different case).
test_case.steps: Enter valid names. Enter the case-variant email. Click Save.
test_case.expected_result: Behaviour is per the documented brand-uniqueness rule (#80). Case-insensitivity is unspecified (RG-11): if uniqueness is intended to be case-insensitive, Save must be blocked as a duplicate; if the case variant is accepted, record it as a potential duplicate-integrity defect and clarification item.

test_case.requirement_reference: Customer Detail §5.1 validations #10/#20, actions #10/#20, §3.1 FormattedCellPhone; FR-09, FR-10, FR-13; RG-04; AS-08
test_case.title: Error guessing — phone entered with formatting characters
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode (AS-03). Probes how the 10-digit-minimum rules and normalisation treat non-digit characters.
test_case.test_data: First = "Mia"; Last = "Fox"; Email = "mia.fox@example.com"; Home Phone = "(202) 555-0100"; Mobile Phone = "202-555-0111".
test_case.steps: Enter valid mandatory fields. Enter Home and Mobile phones containing spaces, parentheses, and dashes. Click Save. Inspect stored values.
test_case.expected_result: Behaviour is per the documented minimum-10-digit rules (#10/#20) and normalisation (actions #10/#20). Character-set handling is unspecified (RG-04): ideally non-digit characters are ignored so the ten digits pass and normalise to "(202) 555-0100" / "(202) 555-0111". If formatting characters cause a false rejection or corrupt storage, record it as a defect/clarification item.

test_case.requirement_reference: Customer Detail §5.1 validation #80, action #8 (CustomerBrand Insert); FR-16, FR-08; RG-13; AS-08
test_case.title: Error guessing — rapid double-click on Save does not create duplicate records
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode (AS-03). Probes the check-then-insert path for duplicate/concurrency protection.
test_case.test_data: First = "Rex"; Last = "Lin"; Email = "rex.lin@example.com" (not yet in the brand).
test_case.steps: Enter valid mandatory fields. Double-click / rapidly click Save twice in succession. Inspect the resulting records.
test_case.expected_result: Exactly one Customer and one CustomerBrand link are created for the email. Duplicate-submit handling is unspecified (RG-13); if two records or two brand links are created, record it as a defect/clarification item.

test_case.requirement_reference: Customer Detail §5.1 validations #50/#60 (name present); §2 (name fields); FR-04, FR-05; RG-10; AS-08
test_case.title: Error guessing — oversized and special-character values in name fields
test_case.preconditions: Account Creation form open in Insert mode (AS-03). Probes robustness of the name-present rules with extreme/special input.
test_case.test_data: First = a 300-character string; Last = "O'Neil-Łukasz <script> 名字"; Email = "long.name@example.com".
test_case.steps: Enter an over-long First Name and a Last Name containing apostrophes, hyphens, accented/non-Latin characters, and markup-like text. Enter a valid Email. Click Save. Inspect stored values and page rendering.
test_case.expected_result: Per §5.1 #50/#60 the names are non-empty, so those validations pass. As no length or character-set constraints are documented (RG-10), record the actual behaviour: input should be stored and rendered safely without truncation surprises, layout breakage, or script execution. Any data corruption, unsafe rendering, or unhandled error is a defect/clarification item.
